title: How to spot a fake natty: Too big too young
summary: NH argues that a teenager who gets very big after a year or so of lifting is almost certainly enhanced, since hypertrophy comes from volume accumulated over years. He explains how these young fake natties hurt impressionable viewers, who end up blaming their genetics or copying bad training, and restates his pro-natural stance.

claims.claim: Years of training don't equal experience; how you apply yourself decides how much knowledge you gain, just like employees with 30 years at a company who have nothing to show for it.
The internet gives quick access to information, but nothing replaces applying it to your own body, because studies may not translate to you.
Steroids remove the need for long training or knowledge, because some muscles grow from hormones alone whether or not you know how to target them.
Every lean, muscular natural he has met was in his late twenties or so and had many years of training behind him.
A 17-18-year-old his size or bigger after a year of lifting is extremely suspicious; even the best genetics have limits on what one year can build, especially mid-puberty.
He started as a skeleton, so it took him a long time just to build a sturdy body; average starters climb faster, but there is a speed limit.
Hypertrophy is a direct result of the volume and tonnage accumulated by a muscle over time: more squats, bigger legs; more curls, bigger biceps.
Studies show PEDs cause hypertrophy without any exercise; you can grow sitting on the couch, depending on dose.
Young fake natties usually teach nothing because they don't know how to train; they sell their image on Instagram and YouTube.
Natural teens comparing themselves to enhanced peers think they're doing something wrong, when they just need patience.
He's glad YouTube fitness didn't exist during his formative years, as it might have discouraged him.
Viewers unaware of PED use either conclude they have bad genetics and give up, or copy the enhanced lifter's training.
Enhanced youngsters often train with lots of cables and few compounds, the opposite of what a natural should do.
Naturals should focus on compound movements, complement them with isolation, and chase progressive overload; it takes years.
Starting PEDs early can give an edge to someone who wants to be a pro bodybuilder, but most such kids don't make it: health gets wrecked, or they find there's no money in bodybuilding and quit.
One enhanced teen influencer can influence a hundred thousand others, some of whom start using, so the cycle repeats endlessly.
He always promotes natural bodybuilding and tells viewers not to use drugs; you don't need them to grow.
